title: PM10 next-hour prediction - Beijing, Aotizhongxin station (UCI)
summary: We predicted PM10 one hour ahead using the Beijing, Aotizhongxin station (UCI) data. XGBoost did best on the validation period, so we used it. On the test period (12 May 2016 to 28 Feb 2017) its average error was 14.842 µg/m³. Just repeating the last hour's value gave 14.962 µg/m³, so the model was 0.8% better. 181 episodes were flagged: 126 look like unusual pollution, 5 look like data problems and 50 are unclear.
how_it_was_made: Read the hourly data and treated empty cells and -200 as missing.

Built the inputs: hour, weekday, the reading 1 hour before, the reading 2 hours before, the reading 3 hours before, the reading at the same time the day before, temperature, air pressure, dew point, rain, wind speed.
Split the timeline in order: first 60% to train, next 20% to choose the model, last 20% to test.
Tried Linear Regression, Random Forest and XGBoost. Each predicts how much the level changes in the next hour.
Flagged test hours where the miss was more than 52.69 µg/m³ (bigger than 95% of the misses on the validation period).
By design this limit flags 5% of the validation hours; on the test period it flagged 4.3% of hours. So the number of episodes partly depends on where the limit is set.

Grouped flagged hours that were less than 3 hours apart and checked each group: missing inputs or a gap, a stuck reading, or a sudden jump that nothing else shared mean a data problem; other pollutants moving the same way at the same time mean unusual pollution; anything else is unclear.
patterns: Most episodes peaked around 00:00, 16:00 and 20:00, and 73% fell on weekdays, about what you'd expect, so they are spread across the week. The busiest month was Nov 2016 with 30 episodes.

most_severe.explanation: Fri 27 Jan 2017 21:00 to Sat 28 Jan 11:00: PM10 was 815.00 µg/m³ at 01:00, but the model expected about 334.58 µg/m³, so it was 480.42 higher. The inputs were complete, and CO, NO2, PM2.5, SO2 and O3 were also unusually high at the same time. These come from separate instruments, so this looks like a real rise in pollution.

Mon 25 Jul 2016, 10:00 to 11:00: PM10 was 450.00 µg/m³ at 10:00, but the model expected about 49.18 µg/m³, so it was 400.82 higher.
